# Person domain: definitions

*Generated by `scripts/generate/definitions.py` from `_person__conceptual.yml`, next to this file. Edit the conceptual model, then run the script; don't edit this file.*

{% docs person %}
**Person.** A human being the university knows, in any role, now or before: one person, however many roles they hold and however many systems record them.

- Business key: The person's own key, given once and never reused. It is no system's number: the numbers the systems give (SIS|S-20436, HR|E-4417) are the person's identifiers. Issued by: Registrar's office.
- Owner of the meaning: Mei Tanaka, registrar's office.
- Identity: Each record a system holds is a person of its own, until a rule or a recorded decision says it's someone already known.
- Identity: A record that holds another system's number is the person that number belongs to. A research record that holds a staff ID is that staff member.
- Identity: Two records are one person only when the registrar's office decides it, or a rule it agreed does. The decision is recorded, with its reason, and can be undone.
- Identity: A decision that two records are different people stops any rule from joining them.
- Identity: Sharing an email or an address doesn't make two records one person.
- Rule: Legal name: from the student system, which checks it against an identity document. Kept by the registrar's office.
- Rule: Preferred name and home address: set by the person, through self-service.
- Rule: Work details: from the HR system. Kept by HR.
- History: Every version of every record is kept. Joining two records into one person, or parting them, is dated and recorded.
- Not in the business glossary: data governance confirmed there's no term for it, on 2026-10-20.
{% enddocs %}

{% docs role %}
**Role.** A part a person plays for the university, for a time: applicant, student, tutor, researcher or alumni. A person can hold several roles at once, and the same role more than once.

- Business key: The record that grants the role, qualified by its key set: a student ID in an award (SIS|S-20436|GCHI), a contract (HR|T-26041), a place on a project (RES|R-3082|RP-26017), an alumni record (ALU|A-61207). Issued by: The system that creates the role.
- Owner of the meaning: Mei Tanaka, registrar's office.
- Kind: applicant. Someone who has applied to study, until the application is decided. Created by the application. Owner: Admissions office.
- Kind: student. Someone learning with the university, in an award or not: the student domain's learner. Created in the student system, or by the learning platforms for a learner with no award. Owner: Mei Tanaka, registrar's office.
- Kind: tutor. Someone who teaches a unit under a contract, one teaching period at a time. Created in the HR system. Owner: HR.
- Kind: researcher. Someone who works on a research project, for the time they're on it. Created in the research system. Owner: Research office.
- Kind: alumni. Someone the university has conferred an award on, from the day it was conferred. Created in the alumni system. Owner: Alumni office.
- Rule: A role starts on a date, and ends on a date once it ends.
- Rule: Each role relates to what it's for: a student role to an award, a tutor role to a unit in a teaching period, a researcher role to a project.
- Rule: The owner of each kind of role decides what it means and who holds it. The registrar's office decides who the person is.
- History: Every role keeps its dates, and every change to them is a new version.
- Not in the business glossary: data governance confirmed there's no term for it, on 2026-10-20.
{% enddocs %}

{% docs contact_point %}
**Contact point.** A way to reach a person, kept for a purpose: an email, a phone number or an address, with what it's for (study, work or personal) and when it was last confirmed.

- Business key: The kind and the value, written one way to be compared, such as an email in lower case.
- Owner of the meaning: Mei Tanaka, registrar's office.
- Rule: Each system writes to the contact point for its purpose. The person decides their personal ones.
- Rule: A contact point can reach more than one person. A shared home address is one contact point, for each person who lives there.
- Rule: A contact point is never the person. Two records that share one aren't one person for that alone.
- History: Every contact point keeps when it was added, last confirmed and closed.
- Not in the business glossary: data governance confirmed there's no term for it, on 2026-10-20.
{% enddocs %}

{% docs identifier %}
**Identifier.** A number a system gives a person, kept with the system that issued it: a student ID, a staff ID, a research member ID, an alumni ID.

- Business key: The number, qualified by the key set of the system that issued it, SIS|S-17142 or HR|E-4417. Issued by: The issuing system.
- Owner of the meaning: Mei Tanaka, registrar's office.
- Rule: A person can have many identifiers, from one system or several. None replaces another.
- Rule: An identifier belongs to one person, and is never given to anyone else.
- Rule: When two records turn out to be one person, both identifiers stay. The issuing system says which one it keeps as its main one.
- Rule: A number one system holds for another (a staff ID in the research system) is the issuer's identifier, not a new one.
- History: An identifier is kept for good, with the day it was issued and, if it's retired, the day it was retired.
- Not in the business glossary: data governance confirmed there's no term for it, on 2026-10-20.
{% enddocs %}
